workshops.physicalJob: Split, bind and fit primitive materials without powered tooling
Strike stone or flint into sharp flakes, heads and points
Shape wood into hafts, staves, stocks and shield bodies
Cure hides and cut or stitch straps, wraps and lining
Weave, pad and stitch processed fiber into equipment panels
Pour molten nonferrous stock into reusable component forms
Heat existing metal stock or worked forms to forging temperature
Hammer heated stock into working heads, blades and fittings
Raise armor plates, form helmets and join mail sections
Cool a heated hardenable ferrous working form; preserve its material identity
Reheat a hardened ferrous form to reduce brittleness where its material supports heat treatment
Cut a working edge or remove forging scale from formed metal
Seal, polish or smooth surfaces where this communicates actual construction
Make and fit joints, guards, grips, sockets and fastening assemblies
Join finished components into the original equipment prefab
Bind special materials or enchant an existing mundane assembly at its original progression station

components.admissionReason: Knapping changes process and supplies reusable cutting and piercing forms
A reusable joining component distinguishes binding from shaping
Reusable forms communicate length and load-bearing construction
Curing, straps and lining are reused across weapon grips, armor and shields
Weaving and padding express the textile technology gate
Heated stock exists only as the input state required by forging; no redundant ore-to-billet tax
Shared small hardware is reused rather than producing an item-specific component for every recipe
Casting provides materially distinct nonferrous heads and fittings
Working geometry distinguishes blade, striking, piercing and digging equipment
Hardened forms express a real ferrous technology gate and are shared by cutting and piercing tools
A usable edge is a distinct transformation from a rough forged or cast form
Plate, helmets and mail require different forming geometry from weapon heads
Batchable ammunition separates reusable shafts and fletching from material-specific heads

routes.materialCondition: Stone/flint edges or primitive bound wood; no metal heating or quenching
Copper/bronze forms suitable for casting; no ferrous hardening requirement
Hardenable ferrous cutting or piercing forms; tempering only where justified by that material
Forged striking heads; no universal cutting-edge heat treatment
Wooden or composite bows, stocks and shields; preserve original advanced station gates
Hide, leather or padded textile garments; no casting or plate forming
Metal helmets, plates, mail or reinforcement; treatment depends on material rather than all armor
Arrow/bolt batches; manufacture heads by their material route and retain native output batch size
Magical, crystal, chitin, bone or current endgame materials; preserve original finished prefab, donor chain and progression station
